1	\section{Discussion and Conclusion}
2	\label{sec:conclusion}
3	
4	We present a controlled comparison demonstrating that the structural pruning criterion shapes post-RLVR recovery capacity.
5	Under identical GRPO training, CKA-only pruning enables active learning (peak reward 4.4$\times$ Standard), while importance-based methods collapse; extended training to 300 steps confirms this gap is structural.
6	We observe evidence consistent with representational diversity playing a role in recovery differences: CKA-only diverges most from the dense representation ($\mu{=}0.62$) yet recovers best, while collapsing methods preserve dense fidelity ($\mu{\geq}0.88$), though causal verification remains for future work.
7	Reward-accuracy decoupling is sparsity-dependent: at 15\%, GRPO amplifies the CKA-only advantage (5.69\,pp$\to$7.20\,pp), while at 20--25\% GRPO cannot improve upon SFT baselines, motivating reward trajectory as the appropriate diagnostic.
8	Cross-scale (1.5B) and cross-architecture (Qwen2.5-Math-7B) experiments provide initial evidence for generality.
9	Recent work shows that RL fine-tuning updates only 5--30\% of parameters~\citep{mukherjee2025rlsubnetworks}; whether CKA-based pruning preferentially preserves structures within this active subnetwork is an open question that would provide a complementary mechanistic explanation.
10	
11	RLVR relies on global exploration~\citep{rlsqueezes2026} requiring diverse computational pathways; gradient importance removes representationally unique structures that provide these pathways, while CKA-based pruning preserves them---echoing the Lottery Ticket Hypothesis~\citep{frankle2019lth} in that the winning subnetwork depends on the training paradigm.
12	Practically, intra-layer CKA overlap ($<$2 min on one GPU) can screen pruning masks for RLVR compatibility before committing to expensive RL training.
13	
14	Code, pruning masks, and model checkpoints will be released upon acceptance.

5	LLM-Pruner~\citep{llmpruner2023} introduced dependency-aware structural pruning for transformers; Bonsai~\citep{bonsai2025} achieves competitive results using only forward passes; GRASPrune~\citep{graspprune2026} advances the state of the art with global gating that jointly prunes FFN channels and KV head groups.

Structured MLP channel pruning of reasoning Large Language Models (LLMs) is typically followed by recovery training---SFT or RLVR---to restore reasoning capabilities.
RLVR is widely considered superior, yet we demonstrate that this hierarchy reflects suboptimal pruning rather than a fundamental property of RL: when pruning preserves representational diversity, recovery method choice becomes irrelevant ($|\Delta(\text{GRPO}-\text{SFT})| \leq 1.14$\,pp across all settings), a phenomenon we term \emph{reward-accuracy decoupling}.
We propose Recovery-Aware Structured Pruning (\rasp{}), which balances gradient importance with CKA-based representational diversity via a coefficient $\alpha$.
A dose-response analysis across $\alpha \in \{0.5, 1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0\}$ on DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B reveals an inverted-U: recovery peaks at $\alpha{=}2.0$ (66.11\% on GSM8K), the optimal balance of importance and diversity.
Under identical GRPO training, importance-dominated pruning ($\alpha{=}1.0$) collapses while diversity-preserving criteria achieve active learning (peak reward 4.4$\times$), forming a \emph{recovery capacity spectrum} that tracks preserved representational diversity.
Cross-scale (1.5B) and cross-architecture (Qwen2.5-Math-7B) experiments provide initial evidence for generality.

\section{Introduction}
\label{sec:intro}

Reasoning Large Language Models can be compressed through structured pruning, but the pruned model must recover its reasoning capabilities through fine-tuning.
The dominant assumption is that the recovery paradigm---SFT versus RLVR---determines recovery quality: \citet{selfhealing2025} demonstrate that RLVR restores pruned reasoning models to near-original accuracy, significantly outperforming SFT.
We show that this hierarchy is an artifact of suboptimal pruning.
When pruning preserves representational diversity, recovery method choice becomes irrelevant: $|\Delta(\text{GRPO}-\text{SFT})| \leq 1.14$\,pp across all pruning criteria and sparsity levels tested.
What determines recovery quality is not \emph{how} you train after pruning, but \emph{which structures} you remove during pruning.

Existing structured pruning methods for reasoning LLMs~\citep{graspprune2026,resp2025,llmpruner2023,bonsai2025} optimize for post-pruning quality without studying how the criterion shapes downstream RL recovery.
\citet{rlsqueezes2026} show that RL and SFT impose fundamentally different demands on model representations---RL compresses incorrect paths while SFT expands correct ones---suggesting that pruning decisions should affect RL trainability.
Yet no prior work has compared multiple pruning criteria under RL or asked whether the ``RLVR $>$ SFT'' advantage persists across pruning strategies.

\begin{figure}[t]
\centering
\includegraphics[width=\columnwidth]{../figures/paper/fig1_dose_response.pdf}
\caption{Dose-response curve for the CKA diversity coefficient $\alpha$ at 20\% MLP channel sparsity on GSM8K ($N{=}1{,}319$). Recovery accuracy follows an inverted-U, peaking at $\alpha{=}2.0$ (66.11\%). SFT and GRPO curves nearly overlap ($|\Delta| \leq 1.14$\,pp at every point), visually demonstrating reward-accuracy decoupling: the pruning criterion---not the recovery paradigm---determines outcome.}
\label{fig:dose_response}
\end{figure}

We present a controlled comparison on DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B~\citep{deepseek2025r1} at 20\% MLP channel sparsity, varying the balance between gradient importance and CKA-based representational diversity~\citep{kornblith2019cka} via a coefficient $\alpha$ in the pruning score (Figure~\ref{fig:dose_response}).
The dose-response curve reveals an inverted-U: recovery peaks at $\alpha{=}2.0$ (66.11\% GRPO on GSM8K~\citep{cobbe2021gsm8k}), where importance and diversity reach optimal balance.
Under identical GRPO~\citep{shao2024grpo} training, four criteria produce a \textbf{recovery capacity spectrum}: CKA-only pruning achieves active learning (peak reward 4.4$\times$ Standard), Random stagnates, Standard (importance-only;~\citealp{llmpruner2023}) exhibits borderline collapse, and $\alpha{=}1.0$ collapses fully.
The ordering tracks preserved representational diversity, not gradient importance.
A depth pruning baseline (ShortGPT;~\citealp{shortgpt2024}) is the only method where GRPO actively degrades accuracy ($-$1.36\,pp), confirming that pruning granularity interacts with RL trainability.

Our contributions are:
\begin{enumerate}[nosep,leftmargin=*]
    \item We discover \textbf{reward-accuracy decoupling}: $|\Delta(\text{GRPO}-\text{SFT})| \leq 1.14$\,pp across all pruning criteria and sparsity levels, demonstrating that recovery method choice is secondary to pruning criterion quality. This decoupling is sparsity-dependent: at 15\%, GRPO amplifies the CKA-guided advantage ($+$1.51\,pp differential; $p{<}0.001$), while at 20--25\% it cannot improve upon SFT baselines (\S\ref{sec:decoupling}).
    \item We propose \textbf{Recovery-Aware Structured Pruning (\rasp{})}, which balances gradient importance with CKA-based representational diversity via a coefficient $\alpha$. A dose-response analysis identifies $\alpha{=}2.0$ as the optimal balance, achieving the highest recovery accuracy (66.11\%) across all criteria tested (\S\ref{sec:scoring}).
    \item We provide comprehensive experimental validation: a \textbf{recovery capacity spectrum} across four criteria with extended training (300 steps), cross-scale (1.5B), cross-architecture (Qwen2.5-Math-7B) generalization, and dose-response causal evidence (\S\ref{sec:recovery_gradient}, \S\ref{sec:extended_analysis}).
\end{enumerate}

1	\section{Introduction}
2	\label{sec:intro}
3	
4	Reasoning Large Language Models can be compressed through structured pruning, but the pruned model must recover its reasoning capabilities through fine-tuning.
5	The dominant assumption is that the recovery paradigm---SFT versus RLVR---determines recovery quality: \citet{selfhealing2025} demonstrate that RLVR restores pruned reasoning models to near-original accuracy, significantly outperforming SFT.

9	
10	Existing structured pruning methods for reasoning LLMs~\citep{graspprune2026,resp2025,llmpruner2023,bonsai2025} optimize for post-pruning quality without studying how the criterion shapes downstream RL recovery.
11	\citet{rlsqueezes2026} show that RL and SFT impose fundamentally different demands on model representations---RL compresses incorrect paths while SFT expands correct ones---suggesting that pruning decisions should affect RL trainability.
12	Yet no prior work has compared multiple pruning criteria under RL or asked whether the ``RLVR $>$ SFT'' advantage persists across pruning strategies.

1	\section{Introduction}
2	\label{sec:intro}
3	
4	Reasoning Large Language Models can be compressed through structured pruning, but the pruned model must recover its reasoning capabilities through fine-tuning.
5	The dominant assumption is that the recovery paradigm---SFT versus RLVR---determines recovery quality: \citet{selfhealing2025} demonstrate that RLVR restores pruned reasoning models to near-original accuracy, significantly outperforming SFT.
6	We show that this hierarchy is an artifact of suboptimal pruning.
7	When pruning preserves representational diversity, recovery method choice becomes irrelevant: $|\Delta(\text{GRPO}-\text{SFT})| \leq 1.14$\,pp across all pruning criteria and sparsity levels tested.
8	What determines recovery quality is not \emph{how} you train after pruning, but \emph{which structures} you remove during pruning.
9	
10	Existing structured pruning methods for reasoning LLMs~\citep{graspprune2026,resp2025,llmpruner2023,bonsai2025} optimize for post-pruning quality without studying how the criterion shapes downstream RL recovery.
11	\citet{rlsqueezes2026} show that RL and SFT impose fundamentally different demands on model representations---RL compresses incorrect paths while SFT expands correct ones---suggesting that pruning decisions should affect RL trainability.
12	Yet no prior work has compared multiple pruning criteria under RL or asked whether the ``RLVR $>$ SFT'' advantage persists across pruning strategies.

1	\section{Discussion and Conclusion}
2	\label{sec:conclusion}
3	
4	We present a controlled comparison demonstrating that the structural pruning criterion shapes post-RLVR recovery capacity.
5	Under identical GRPO training, CKA-only pruning enables active learning (peak reward 4.4$\times$ Standard), while importance-based methods collapse; extended training to 300 steps confirms this gap is structural.
6	We observe evidence consistent with representational diversity playing a role in recovery differences: CKA-only diverges most from the dense representation ($\mu{=}0.62$) yet recovers best, while collapsing methods preserve dense fidelity ($\mu{\geq}0.88$), though causal verification remains for future work.
7	Reward-accuracy decoupling is sparsity-dependent: at 15\%, GRPO amplifies the CKA-only advantage (5.69\,pp$\to$7.20\,pp), while at 20--25\% GRPO cannot improve upon SFT baselines, motivating reward trajectory as the appropriate diagnostic.
8	Cross-scale (1.5B) and cross-architecture (Qwen2.5-Math-7B) experiments provide initial evidence for generality.
9	Recent work shows that RL fine-tuning updates only 5--30\% of parameters~\citep{mukherjee2025rlsubnetworks}; whether CKA-based pruning preferentially preserves structures within this active subnetwork---consistent with the Lottery Ticket Hypothesis~\citep{frankle2019lth}---is an open question that would provide a complementary mechanistic explanation.
